findings.description: The database username and password are rendered into EC2 user data and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data and the resulting local file can expose reusable database credentials to parties able to read instance metadata, launch configuration state, or obtain host access.

The RDS instance is configured with publicly_accessible = true, assigning it a public network endpoint. Although the shown security-group ingress is VPC-scoped, this unnecessarily exposes the database to public-network attack paths and weakens network segmentation.
storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, so RDS storage, backups, and snapshots are not encrypted at rest.

The EC2-attached role is granted s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* over every resource. A compromise of catalog_app_server would yield broad account-level access, including likely privilege-escalation and data-access paths.

MySQL access is allowed from the entire portal VPC CIDR rather than being limited to the application security group or specific required hosts. Any compromised or unauthorized workload in that VPC can attempt to reach the database on port 3306.
